name.definition: A name is what a person, place, or thing is called or how it is identified.

narrative.definition: A narrative tells events in a set order.

narrow.definition: If something is narrow, it is not wide; it is thin.

nation.definition: A nation is a country or a political entity.
nation.sentence: Mexico is a nation of emigrants.

national.definition: If something is national it affects a whole nation or country.

native.definition: If something is native, it belongs to you by birth.

natural.definition: Something is natural if people didn't make it.
natural.sentence: Animals, plants and rocks are natural things.

naturally.definition: If something happens naturally, it happens in a natural manner without special intervention.
naturally.sentence: Naturally, the lawyer sent us a huge bill.

nature.sentence: We went on a nature walk.

near.sentence: It was a near miss, but the car didn't hit us.

nearly.definition: If something is nearly it is close to be true, but not true.
nearly.sentence: We were nearly hit by the car, but got out of its way just in time.

necessarily.definition: If something is not necessarily true, it may or may not be true.
necessarily.sentence: I know we don't have a car, but that's not necessarily a problem.

necessary.definition: Something is necessary if people need it. It must happen or there will be a big problem.
necessary.sentence: It's necessary to stop when you see a red light.

neck.definition: The part of the body between the head and the torso.
neck.sentence: He admired her long graceful neck.

need.definition: If you need something, you want it and must have it.
need.sentence: Sir, you need to leave now.

negative.definition: If something is negative, it is harmful, sad, or otherwise not good.
negative.sentence: You can believe or not believe, that there's a positive and negative side to everything.

neglect.definition: If you neglect someone, you do not take care of them.

negotiate.definition: If you negotiate with somebody about something, you each give your own ideas and try to reach an agreement.
negotiate.sentence: He made it clear that he would not negotiate.

negotiation.definition: Negotiation is a process of achieving and agreement between two or more people through a discussion.
negotiation.sentence: The buyout negotiation lasted several days.

neighbor.sentence: Fort Worth is a neighbor of Dallas.

neighborhood.definition: A neighborhood is part of a town or city.
neighborhood.sentence: They live in an Italian neighborhood on the west side of the city.

neither.definition: Neither is used to show that a something that is not true in one case is also not true in another case.
neither.sentence: She didn't have one, and neither did I.

nerve.definition: A nerve is a cell in the body that sends signals. The brain is made of nerves.
nerve.sentence: He didn't have the nerve to ask her to dance.

nervous.definition: If you are nervous, you are tense and worried about something.
nervous.sentence: I am nervous about my examinations.

net.definition: A net is a thing made of ropes or string that lets small things through but keeps big things in.
net.sentence: I forgot my fishing net. What will we use to catch fish now?

network.definition: A network is a group of connections between a number of points.
network.sentence: Electronic systems control the busiest parts of the rail network.

never.definition: If something never happens, it does not happen at any time.
never.sentence: As a child I was told that I should never tell a lie.

nevertheless.definition: You use nevertheless to add surprising information or something in contrast to what was already said or written.
nevertheless.sentence: We are seriously over budget. I have nevertheless decided to continue with the project.

new.definition: If something is new, it is not old.

newly.definition: If something is newly formed, discovered, arrived, etc., then the changed happened not long before.
newly.sentence: The female insect deposits its eggs on the newly formed fruit.

news.definition: News is information about things that happened a short time ago, especially on the radio, TV or in newspapers.
news.sentence: Did you hear the news that the war just ended?

newspaper.definition: A newspaper is something you read for the news. It is usually published on cheap paper.
newspaper.sentence: He read his newspaper at breakfast.

next.definition: Immediately following in time or order.

nice.definition: If something is nice, it's good and people probably like it.
nice.sentence: I didn't know him, but I hear he was a very nice man.

no.definition: Used to disagree or refuse; to say something different from what the other person said.

nobody.definition: A nobody is a person who is not important.

noise.definition: A noise is a sound, usually one that you don't want.
noise.sentence: There's too much noise. I can't hear what she's saying.

none.definition: A canonical hour that is the ninth hour of the day counting from sunrise.

nor.definition: Nor is used to show that a something that is not true in one case is also not true in another case.
nor.sentence: I don't belong here, and nor do you.

normal.definition: A normal thing, or situation, is one that is not special.
normal.sentence: A normal computer has a keyboard and a screen.

normally.definition: You use normally to show what usually happens or what you usually do.
normally.sentence: The car is working normally now.

north.definition: North is the direction towards the top of the Earth, opposite to south; If you are looking north, the sun sets on your left.
north.sentence: Canada is the biggest country in North America.

northern.definition: If something is northern, it is in, from, or about the north.
northern.sentence: We couldn't go south, so we looked for a more northern route.

nose.definition: The part of the face that sticks out and is used for breathing and smelling things.

not.definition: "Not" makes a phrase have the opposite meaning.

note.definition: A note is a single sound in music.
note.sentence: In this song, every word is on a different note.

nothing.definition: A quantity of no importance; thing (object:), singular, negative pronoun; pronoun, thing, singular; quantifier: negative existential.
nothing.sentence: It looked like nothing I had ever seen before.

notice.definition: If you notice something, you become aware of it.
notice.sentence: You didn't even notice that I cut my hair.

notion.definition: A notion is an idea about something.
notion.sentence: We have to reject this strange notion that some languages are better than others.

noun.definition: A noun is a kind of word that is usually the name of a person, place, thing, quality, or idea. In English, nouns can be the subject or object of a sentence. They can be singular or plural.

novel.definition: Something that is novel is new and interesting.
novel.sentence: The computer produced a completely novel proof of a well-known theorem.

now.definition: In the historical present; at this point in the narration of a series of past events.
now.sentence: President Kennedy now calls in the National Guard.

nowadays.definition: Now and recently; in this time.
nowadays.sentence: Back then we walked everywhere, but nowadays everyone drives a car.

number.definition: A symbol that that is used to describe quantity; a numeral.
number.sentence: She has a number of dictionaries--four or five, I think.

numerous.definition: If something is numerous, it is in large amount.
numerous.sentence: Why are there numerous ants here?

nurse.definition: A nurse is a healthcare worker who helps doctors and helps sick or injured people with the activities of daily life.
